Let
\[
m=\binom n2,\qquad \lambda=2n-2.
\]
The Laplacian of \(T_n\) has degree \(2(n-2)\). If \(B\) is the \(n\times m\) unsigned incidence matrix of \(K_n\), so the column for \(\{i,j\}\) is \(e_i+e_j\), then
\[
A(T_n)=B^TB-2I,
\]
hence
\[
L=2(n-2)I-A(T_n)=2(n-1)I-B^TB=\lambda I-B^TB.
\]

Over \(\mathbb Q\), the eigenvalues of \(L\) are
\[
0\quad(1\text{ time}),\qquad n\quad(n-1\text{ times}),\qquad \lambda\quad\left(m-n\text{ times}\right).
\]
Thus
\[
|K(T_n)|=\frac{n^{\,n-1}\lambda^{\,m-n}}{m}
=n^{n-2}(2n-2)^{m-n}.
\]

It remains to determine the Smith factors.

Let \(C=\mathbb Z^{E(K_n)}\), and define
\[
s:C\to \mathbb Z^n,\qquad s(\{i,j\})=e_i+e_j.
\]
Then \(B=s\), \(B^T=s^T\), and
\[
L=\lambda I-s^Ts.
\]

For primes \(p\mid n\), \(\lambda\) is a unit \(p\)-adically. The only \(p\)-torsion comes from the induced map on \(s(C)\). Since \(n\) is odd,
\[
s(C)=\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:\sum_i x_i\equiv 0\pmod 2\}.
\]
On this lattice,
\[
sLs^{-1}(y)=ny-\left(\sum_i y_i\right)\mathbf 1.
\]
Its image inside \(\{\sum_i y_i=0\}\) consists exactly of the vectors whose coordinates are all congruent modulo \(n\). Therefore the quotient has Smith form
\[
(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^{n-2}.
\]

For primes \(p\mid \lambda\), we have \(p\nmid n\). The \(n\)-eigenspace contributes no \(p\)-torsion, and the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace has rank
\[
m-n=\binom n2-n=\frac{n(n-3)}2.
\]
Hence the \(p\)-primary part is
\[
(\mathbb Z/\lambda\mathbb Z)^{m-n}
\]
at all primes dividing \(\lambda\).

Because \(n\) is odd,
\[
\gcd(n,\lambda)=\gcd(n,2n-2)=1.
\]
So the \(n\)-part and the \(\lambda\)-part combine into invariant factors by pairing the \(n-2\) copies of \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) with \(n-2\) copies of \(\mathbb Z/\lambda\mathbb Z\). Since
\[
m-n-(n-2)=\frac{n(n-3)}2-(n-2)=\frac{(n-1)(n-4)}2,
\]
the invariant-factor decomposition is
\[
\boxed{
K(T_n)\cong
\left(\mathbb Z/(2n-2)\mathbb Z\right)^{\frac{(n-1)(n-4)}2}
\oplus
\left(\mathbb Z/\bigl(n(2n-2)\bigr)\mathbb Z\right)^{n-2}
}.
\]

The order of this group is
\[
(2n-2)^{\frac{(n-1)(n-4)}2}
\bigl(n(2n-2)\bigr)^{n-2}
=
n^{n-2}(2n-2)^{\frac{n(n-3)}2},
\]
matching the Matrix-Tree eigenvalue check.
